title: Java: reading 1,000,000 rows, shared strings
dataset: The 1M-row write benchmark dataset (10 columns per row: integers, strings (one unique per row), floats, a date/time and a boolean), written by Hypaxel with a shared string table (43.0 MB, 1M distinct strings)
method: Each reader streams the first worksheet and visits every cell with its typed accessors; all must produce the same checksum (10,000,000 cells, sum of all numbers and date serials, 42,833,558 characters of text, 500,000 TRUEs). Time: mean of 5 runs after 2 warm-ups in one JVM. Allocated: bytes allocated by the reading thread per run. Peak RSS: a separate single read in a fresh JVM with default settings. The machine was otherwise idle.
versions: Apache POI 6.0.0 (XSSFReader with a SAX handler and ReadOnlySharedStringsTable)
notes: Hypaxel creates shared strings once, when the table is loaded. Numbers, booleans and dates allocate nothing.

All three readers stream with bounded live memory: each completes with -Xmx16m on the inline file and with -Xmx96m on the shared one, whose string table must be held. The RSS differences come from garbage that the JVM lets accumulate between collections under default settings.
FastExcel did not read number formats (its default); Hypaxel and the POI handler detect date formats.
About 25% of Hypaxel's time is inflate and CRC-32 verification in the JDK.
